No Credo-specific news (press release, 8-K, analyst action) was found for Friday; the only filings were routine insider Form 4/144s.
Why chip stocks rose on Friday was not established from a tier-1/2 source in this research.

Bigger picture (why the stock is ~29% below its June high): the 2026-09-02 ~20% plunge after Q1 results, attributed to GAAP gross-margin compression (68.2% to 64.5%), rising operating costs, and customer concentration (top two customers 61% of revenue) at a high valuation.

Basic driver: Credo's sales depend on a handful of hyperscalers' data-center build plans; when investors worry one of them could slow or switch suppliers, they pay a lower multiple of earnings even while revenue is still growing fast. The non-GAAP margin barely moved (68.3% to 68.0%), so the GAAP drop likely reflects acquisition-related costs rather than weaker pricing.

products.name: Active Electrical Cables (AECs), branded ZeroFlap AECs
products.what_it_is: Copper cables with small signal-boosting chips (retimers/DSPs) built into each end, used to connect servers and switches inside AI data-center racks at 400G-1.6T speeds.
products.analogy: Like a garden hose with a booster pump at each end: plain copper is cheap but loses pressure (signal) over distance; the chips restore it so the cable can be longer and thinner.
products.buyers: Hyperscale cloud companies and 'neo-cloud' AI providers (management cited engagement with five hyperscalers); actual customer names are not disclosed by Credo. Tier-3 analyst coverage cites design wins at Microsoft and Amazon (unconfirmed by the company).
products.how_it_works: Credo designs the chips and sells the finished cable (product revenue); cheaper and lower-power than optical links over short distances (a few meters), more reliable ('ZeroFlap' refers to avoiding link drop-outs).
products.sales: Not disclosed separately. Proxy (labelled): AECs are Credo's largest business per management; total company revenue was $479.0 million in Q1 FY2027. Management said AEC revenue 'more than tripled' in fiscal 2026 (transcript summary, tier 3).
products.size_for_company: Largest product line (exact share not disclosed)
products.competition: Marvell (including its 'Golden Cable' ecosystem), Broadcom, Astera Labs (reportedly pricing lower), cable makers such as Amphenol; long-term threat from co-packaged/near-packaged optics replacing copper (tier-3 analysis).
products.why_investors_care: It is the engine of the 100%+ growth; its future depends on copper staying the cheaper choice inside racks as speeds rise.
products.watch_next: Q2 FY27 results (est. 2026-12-02): AEC customer count, 1.6T ramps, any change in the top-customer mix.

products.name: Optical portfolio: optical DSPs, ZeroFlap optical transceivers, silicon-photonics PICs (from DustPhotonics)
products.what_it_is: Chips and modules that turn electrical signals into light for longer links between racks; the DSP cleans up the signal, the PIC is the light-handling chip.
products.analogy: If AECs are the hallway wiring inside one building, optics are the fiber line between buildings.
products.buyers: Optical module makers and hyperscalers/neo-clouds (names not disclosed).
products.how_it_works: Sells DSP chips and PICs to module makers, and complete ZeroFlap optical modules; aims to bundle DSP + PIC + firmware/telemetry.
products.sales: Guidance, not actual: management expects more than $600 million of optical revenue in fiscal 2027, with ZeroFlap optics, silicon-photonics PICs and optical DSPs each above $100 million. Q1 FY27: record optical DSP revenue and first PIC revenue (amounts not disclosed).
products.stage: Early ramp (production shipments of ZeroFlap optics; first PIC revenue in Q1 FY27)
products.size_for_company: Guided >$600M vs fiscal-2027 total implied by '>85% growth' on ~$1.3B FY26 (inference: roughly a quarter of FY27 revenue)
products.competition: Marvell and Broadcom (incumbent optical DSP leaders), plus other silicon-photonics suppliers.
products.why_investors_care: It is Credo's hedge against the shift from copper to optics and the source of most of the expected second-half acceleration.
products.watch_next: Whether Q2/Q3 results show the optical ramp on track to the >$600M target.
